\[
I_{\text{out}} = \min\!\left(255,\ \max\!\left(0,\ 255\,\frac{I - p_{\text{lo}}}{p_{\text{hi}} - p_{\text{lo}}}\right)\right),
\qquad
p_{\text{lo}} = P_{ 1 }(I),\ p_{\text{hi}} = P_{ 99 }(I)
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(I\): Input value from 0 to 255
- \(P_q\): The q-th percentile of the image values
- \(p_{\text{lo}}, p_{\text{hi}}\): The values that map to 0 and 255

P_q is the q-th percentile of the image values, rounded to the levels 0 to 255. It uses the linear rule of numpy.percentile: the sorted values are indexed from 0 to N - 1, and position (N - 1) q / 100 is interpolated between its two neighbors. The low percentile maps to 0, the high one to 255, and the line between them is clipped at both ends. Percentiles 0 and 100 give min-max normalization. When p_hi is not above p_lo, as in a flat image, the image stays as it is. Values between two levels take the output interpolated between them.
